title: English for Oil & Gas Industry
overview: English for Oil & Gas Industry is a specialized language program designed to strengthen the practical English communication skills required in upstream, midstream, and downstream operations. Participants develop the vocabulary, reading, listening, speaking, and writing abilities needed to understand technical information, communicate with multidisciplinary teams, report operational issues, and participate safely and effectively in routine workplace interactions. The course uses authentic industry scenarios while remaining a language-development program rather than a technical qualification.
audience: Oil and gas technicians, operators, engineers, maintenance personnel, HSE staff, field supervisors, logistics and procurement personnel, administrative support staff, and professionals who need to communicate in English within petroleum-industry workplaces.
methodology: Interactive language workshops, guided vocabulary practice, listening and reading exercises, workplace role-plays, simulated shift handovers and toolbox talks, technical-document interpretation, short report-writing tasks, pronunciation coaching, pair and group activities, and ongoing formative assessment using realistic oil and gas scenarios.
competencies: Clear verbal communication in operational settings
Reading and interpreting common workplace documents
Professional technical writing and incident reporting
objectives: Use essential English terminology for oil and gas facilities, processes, equipment, and job roles.
Understand and communicate routine operational instructions, work updates, and technical descriptions.
Read basic technical documents, procedures, work permits, signs, and safety notices accurately.
Participate in toolbox talks, meetings, and shift handovers using clear and concise English.
Ask for clarification, confirm understanding, and communicate hazards or abnormal conditions appropriately.
Write short operational emails, maintenance updates, log entries, and incident descriptions.
Apply appropriate pronunciation, listening, and professional communication techniques in realistic workplace scenarios.
